readings.title: The Command to Destroy Amalek
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's judgment is pronounced through Samuel.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:1] And Shemu’ěl said to Sha’ul, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent me to anoint you sovereign over <dn>His</dn> people, over Yisra’ěl. And now, listen to the voice of the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> shall punish <dn>את</dn> Amalěq for what he did to Yisra’ěl, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Mitsrayim.</dq> [3] <dq>Now go, and you shall strike <dn>את</dn> Amalěq and put under the ban <dn>את</dn> all that he has, and you shall not spare them, and put to death from man to woman, from infant to nursing child, from ox to sheep, from camel to donkey.’</dq> ”

readings.title: Saul's Partial Obedience
readings.subtitle: He spares King Agag and the best of the livestock.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:4] Then Sha’ul summoned <dn>את</dn> the people and mustered them in Tela’im, two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Yehuḏah. [5] And Sha’ul came to a city of Amalěq, and lay in wait in the wadi. [6] And Sha’ul said to the Qěynites, “Go, turn aside, come down from among the Amalěqites, lest I destroy you with them. For you did show loving-commitment to all the children of Yisra’ěl when they came up out of Mitsrayim.” So the Qěynites turned aside from the midst of the Amalěqites. [7] And Sha’ul struck <dn>את</dn> the Amalěqites, from Ḥavilah all the way to Shur, which is before Mitsrayim. [8] And he caught <dn>את</dn> Aḡaḡ sovereign of the Amalěqites alive, and put under the ban <dn>את</dn> all the people with the edge of the sword. [9] But Sha’ul and the people spared Aḡaḡ and the best of the sheep, and the cattle, and the fatlings, and the lambs, and all that was good, and would not put them under the ban. But all goods despised and worthless, that they put <dn>את</dn> under the ban.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Grief and Samuel's Confrontation
readings.subtitle: Saul's excuse is met with Samuel's pointed questions.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:10] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Shemu’ěl, saying, [11] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am grieved that <dn>I</dn> have set up Sha’ul as sovereign, for he has turned back from following <dn>Me</dn>, and has not performed <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> words.”</dq> And it displeased Shemu’ěl, and he cried to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all night. [12] And Shemu’ěl rose early in the morning to meet Sha’ul, and it was told to Shemu’ěl, saying, “Sha’ul went to Karmel, and see, he set up a monument for himself, then turned and passed over, and went down to Gilgal.” [13] And Shemu’ěl came to Sha’ul, and Sha’ul said to him, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! <dn>I</dn> have performed <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [14] But Shemu’ěl said, “What then is this bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the lowing of the cattle which I hear?” [15] And Sha’ul said, “They have brought them from Amalěq, because the people spared the best of the sheep and the cattle, to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And the rest we have put <dn>את</dn> under the ban.” [16] And Shemu’ěl said to Sha’ul, “Wait, and let me declare to you <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me last night.” And he said to him, “Speak.”

readings.title: The Rebuke: Obedience Over Sacrifice
readings.subtitle: Samuel declares that rebellion is as the sin of divination.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:17] And Shemu’ěl said, “Though you were little in your own eyes, were you not head of the tribes of Yisra’ěl? And did not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> anoint you sovereign over Yisra’ěl? [18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent you on the way, and said, ‘Go, and you shall put under the ban <dn>את</dn> the sinners, <dn>את</dn> the Amalěqites, and fight against them until they are consumed.’ [19] “And why did you not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but swooped down on the spoil, and did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [20] And Sha’ul said to Shemu’ěl, “<dn>I</dn> did obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> went on the way on which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent me, and brought back <dn>את</dn> Aḡaḡ sovereign of Amalěq, and <dn>I</dn> put <dn>את</dn> Amalěq under the ban. [21] “But the people took of the spoil, of the sheep and cattle, the best of that which should have been put under the ban, to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in Gilgal.” [22] Then Shemu’ěl said, “Does <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> delight in ascending offerings and slaughterings, as in obeying the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? Look, to obey is better than a slaughtering, to heed is better than the fat of rams. [23] “For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as wickedness and idolatry. Because you have rejected <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> also does reject you as sovereign.”

readings.title: Saul's Confession and Plea
readings.subtitle: He admits his sin but is more concerned with his honor.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:24] And Sha’ul said to Shemu’ěl, “<dn>I</dn> have sinned, for <dn>I</dn> have transgressed <dn>את</dn> the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> your words, because <dn>I</dn> feared <dn>את</dn> the people and listened to their voice. [25] “And now, please pardon <dn>את</dn> my sin, and return with me, and let me bow myself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [26] But Shemu’ěl said to Sha’ul, “<dn>I</dn> do not return with you, for you have rejected <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does reject you from being sovereign over Yisra’ěl.” [27] And as Shemu’ěl turned around to go away, Sha’ul took hold of the edge of his robe, and it tore. [28] And Shemu’ěl said to him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has torn <dn>את</dn> the reign of Yisra’ěl from you today, and has given it to a neighbour of yours, better than you. [29] “Moreover, the Eminence of Yisra’ěl does not lie nor relent. For <dn>He</dn> is not a man, that <dn>He</dn> should relent.” [30] Then he said, “<dn>I</dn> have sinned. But esteem me now, please, before the elders of my people and before Yisra’ěl, and return with me, and <dn>I</dn> shall bow myself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.” [31] And Shemu’ěl turned back after Sha’ul, and Sha’ul bowed himself to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Execution of Agag and the Final Parting
readings.subtitle: Samuel carries out YeHoVaH's command and mourns for Saul.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 15:32] And Shemu’ěl said, “Bring <dn>את</dn> Aḡaḡ sovereign of the Amalěqites here to me.” So Aḡaḡ came to him delightedly, and Aḡaḡ said, “Truly, the bitterness of death has turned aside.” [33] And Shemu’ěl said, “As your sword bereaved women, let your mother be bereaved among women too.” Shemu’ěl then hewed <dn>את</dn> Aḡaḡ to pieces before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Gilgal. [34] And Shemu’ěl went to Ramah, while Sha’ul went up to his house at Giḇ‛ah of Sha’ul. [35] And Shemu’ěl did not see <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul again until the day of his death, for Shemu’ěl mourned for Sha’ul. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was grieved that <dn>He</dn> had made Sha’ul to reign over Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Samuel Sent to Bethlehem
readings.subtitle: Under the guise of a sacrifice, Samuel seeks Israel's next king.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“How long are you going to mourn for Sha’ul, seeing <dn>I</dn> have rejected him from reigning over Yisra’ěl? Fill <dn>את</dn> your horn with oil, and go, <dn>I</dn> am sending you to Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite. For <dn>I</dn> have seen among his sons a sovereign for <dn>Myself</dn>.”</dq> [2] And Shemu’ěl said, “How would I go? When Sha’ul hears it, he shall kill me.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Take a heifer with you, and say, ‘<dn>I</dn> have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq> [3] <dq>“And you shall invite Yishai to the slaughtering, then let <dn>Me</dn> show you what to do. And you shall anoint for <dn>Me</dn> <dn>את</dn> the one <dn>I</dn> say to you.”</dq> [4] And Shemu’ěl did what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, and went to Běyth Leḥem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, “Do you come in peace?” [5] And he said, “In peace. <dn>I</dn> have come to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Set yourselves apart, and you shall come with me to the slaughtering.” And he set <dn>את</dn> Yishai and <dn>את</dn> his sons apart, and invited them to the slaughtering.

readings.title: David Anointed as King
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH looks at the heart and chooses the youngest son of Jesse.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:6] And it came to be, when they came, that he saw <dn>את</dn> Eliyaḇ and thought, “The anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is indeed before <dn>Him</dn>.” [7] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because <dn>I</dn> have refused him, for not as man sees, for man looks at the eyes, but <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looks at the heart.”</dq> [8] Then Yishai called Aḇinaḏaḇ, and made him pass before Shemu’ěl. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [9] Next Yishai made Shammah pass by. And he said, “Neither has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chosen this one.” [10] And Yishai made seven of his sons pass before Shemu’ěl. And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not chosen these.” [11] And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “Are these all the young men?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, and see, he is tending the sheep.” And Shemu’ěl said to Yishai, “Send and bring him, for we do not turn round till he comes here.” [12] And he sent and brought him in. And he was ruddy, with bright eyes, and handsome. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Arise, anoint him, for this is the one!”</dq> [13] And Shemu’ěl took <dn>את</dn> the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Daviḏ from that day and onwards. And Shemu’ěl arose and went to Ramah.

readings.title: David Enters Saul's Service
readings.subtitle: A skilled musician is sought to soothe the king's troubled spirit.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 16:14] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> turned aside from Sha’ul, and an evil spirit from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> troubled him. [15] And the servants of Sha’ul said to him, “Look, now, an evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is troubling you. [16] “Please, let our master command your servants who are before you, to seek out a man who is a skilled player on the lyre. And it shall be that when the evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> is upon you, that he shall play with his hand, and you be well.” [17] And Sha’ul said to his servants, “Please get me a man that plays well, and bring him to me.” [18] And one of the servants answered and said, “Look, I have seen a son of Yishai the Běyth Leḥemite, who knows how to play, a brave one, and a man of battle, and skilled in words, and a handsome man. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with him.” [19] So Sha’ul sent messengers to Yishai, and said, “Send me <dn>את</dn> your son Daviḏ, who is with the sheep.” [20] And Yishai took a donkey loaded with bread, and a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by his son Daviḏ to Sha’ul. [21] And Daviḏ came to Sha’ul and stood before him. And he loved him greatly, and he became his armour-bearer. [22] Sha’ul therefore sent to Yishai, saying, “Please let Daviḏ stand before me, for he has found favour in my eyes.” [23] And it came to be, whenever the evil spirit from <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon Sha’ul, that Daviḏ would take <dn>את</dn> a lyre and play it with his hand. Then Sha’ul would become refreshed and well, and the evil spirit would leave him.

readings.title: Goliath's Challenge
readings.subtitle: The Philistine champion taunts the armies of Israel.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:1] And the Philistines had gathered <dn>את</dn> their armies for battle, and came together at Soḵoh, which belongs to Yehuḏah, and encamped between Soḵoh and Azěqah, in Ephes Dammim. [2] And Sha’ul and the men of Yisra’ěl were gathered and encamped in the Valley of Ělah, and drew up in battle array to meet the Philistines. [3] And the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, and Yisra’ěl stood on a mountain on the other side, with the valley between them. [4] Then a champion came out from the camp of the Philistines, named Golyath, from Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span. [5] And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was armed with a scaled armour, and the weight of the coat was five thousand sheqels of bronze, [6] and bronze shin guards on his legs and a bronze spear between his shoulders. [7] And the wood of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and his iron spearhead weighed six hundred sheqels, and a shield-bearer went before him. [8] And he stood and shouted to the armies of Yisra’ěl, and said to them, “Why have you come out to line up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and you the servants of Sha’ul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me. [9] “If he is able to fight with me, and shall strike me, then we shall be your servants. But if I overcome him and shall strike him, then you shall be our servants and serve us.” [10] Then the Philistine said, “This day <dn>I</dn> shall reproach <dn>את</dn> the armies of Yisra’ěl. Give me a man, and let us fight together.” [11] And Sha’ul and all Yisra’ěl heard <dn>את</dn> these words of the Philistine, and they were broken down and in great fear.

readings.title: David Sent to the Battlefront
readings.subtitle: Jesse sends his youngest son with provisions for his brothers.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:12] Now Daviḏ was the son of that Ephrathite of Běyth Leḥem in Yehuḏah, whose name was Yishai, and he had eight sons, and in the days of Sha’ul the man was old among men. [13] And the three oldest sons of Yishai went, they had gone to follow Sha’ul to the battle, and the names of his three sons who went to the battle were Eliyaḇ the first-born, and his second Aḇinaḏaḇ, and the third Shammah. [14] And Daviḏ was the youngest. And the three oldest followed Sha’ul, [15] but Daviḏ went and returned from Sha’ul to feed <dn>את</dn> his father’s sheep at Běyth Leḥem. [16] And for forty days the Philistine drew near, morning and evening, and took his stand. [17] Then Yishai said to his son Daviḏ, “Please take to your brothers an ěphah of this dried grain and these ten loaves, and run to your brothers at the camp. [18] “And take <dn>את</dn> these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand, and see <dn>את</dn> how your brothers are, and bring back <dn>את</dn> news of them.” [19] For Sha’ul and they and all the men of Yisra’ěl were in the Valley of Ělah, fighting with the Philistines.

readings.title: David Hears the Challenge
readings.subtitle: His inquiry about the reward is met with his brother's scorn.
readings.text: [1 Samuel 17:20] And Daviḏ rose up early in the morning, and left <dn>את</dn> the sheep with a herdsman, and took and went as Yishai had commanded him. And he came to the camp as the army was going out to the fight, and they shouted for the battle. [21] And Yisra’ěl and the Philistines drew up in battle array, army against army. [22] And Daviḏ left <dn>את</dn> his supplies in the hand of the keeper of the supplies, and ran to the army, and came and greeted his brothers. [23] And he was speaking with them and saw the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Golyath by name, coming up from the armies of the Philistines. And he spoke according to the same words, and Daviḏ heard. [24] And all the men of Yisra’ěl, when they saw the man, ran from him and were in great fear. [25] And the men of Yisra’ěl said, “Have you seen this man who has come up? For he has come up to reproach Yisra’ěl. And it shall be that the man who strikes him, the sovereign is going to enrich him with great riches, and give him his daughter, and give <dn>את</dn> his father’s house exemption in Yisra’ěl.” [26] And Daviḏ spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, “What shall be done for the man who strikes <dn>את</dn> this Philistine and shall take away reproach from Yisra’ěl? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should reproach the armies of the living <dn>Elohim</dn>?” [27] And the people answered him according to this word, saying, “This is what is done for the man who strikes him.” [28] And Eliyaḇ his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men. And Eliyaḇ’s displeasure burned against Daviḏ, and he said, “Why did you come down here? And with whom have you left <dn>את</dn> those few sheep in the wilderness? <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> your pride and <dn>את</dn> the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle.” [29] And Daviḏ said, “Now what have I done? Was it not but a word?” [30] And he turned around from him toward another and said the same word. And these people answered him a word like the first word. [31] And when the words which Daviḏ spoke were heard, they reported them to Sha’ul, and he sent for him.
